She lies down the moment she sees you with a brush.|The hippogriff has kept her muddiest wing for you, and holds it out like a gift.} {season == "autumn": Leaves are stuck in her feathers.|{The stable cat supervises from a beam.|The owls are watching to see if you get it wrong.|Brask is somewhere nearby, humming to a feed sack.}} Groom her properly, feather by feather {It takes the whole afternoon and both your arms. She falls asleep with her head on your boot, which is the highest mark a hippogriff gives.|You do it the slow way, with the grain. She clicks her beak at you every time you're right, and once, gently, when you're wrong.|You know her feathers now. She lets you do the hard bit under the wing, and Brask, passing, says nothing at all.} Read Brask's grooming notes on the wall {The notes are long, opinionated and illustrated. You learn a great deal about feathers. The hippogriff stays muddy and sighs at you.|You read the notes. Brask catches you at it and says, "She doesn't need a scholar, she needs a brush."|You finish the notes, which you could recite by now, and leave the brush for someone else. The hippogriff looks away.}
